about.heading: About
about.body: YGO Omega is an automatic (and manual) Yu-Gi-Oh Trading Card Game simulator developed by Duelists Unite (DU). It has all of the cards for free with an automatic Swiss Tournament system and ranking. The DU discord hosts weekly tournaments with prizes and even casual players with beginner knowledge of Yu-Gi-Oh can find something to enjoy!

method.title: How it’s counted
method.model: Every game with a result fits one model: each deck has a strength, and the chance of winning a game depends on the two strengths, on who went first and on the rating gap. Strengths are pulled toward the ladder mean, so a deck with few games sits near the middle. The expected win rate is that strength against the field, weighted by share; its 95% interval is widened by how much the deck’s daily results move beyond chance. Tier reads the expected rate against fixed marks: T1 from 55%, T1.5 from 54%, T2 from 52.5%, T3 from 51%, T4 from 50%, none under 0.5% of the meta or 10 duelists.
method.matchups: A matchup starts from what the two strengths predict and moves toward the observed games only as far as the sample allows, so a pair with 20 games stays near its prediction. It is called favorable or unfavorable only when its interval excludes the prediction. Under {min} games a matchup is hidden unless you ask for it. A week is a block of 7 days from the season’s start; a deck is flagged as changed only past 3.5 standard errors.
method.bands: A game belongs to one rating band: the one of its two players’ mean rating the day before, each capped at the rating cap, so a mismatched pair lands between them. The page opens on {floor} and up; All ratings holds every band from Bronze.
method.filters: Left out this season: games of players with too few ranked games ({players}), games of one-off decklists ({lists}) and games whose mean rating is Iron ({iron}), of {total} games.
method.caveats: Read with care: after game 1 the loser picks who goes first, so turn order is only shown for game 1; a card’s effect compares lists with and without it, which is not the same as cutting it from your list; a deck whose games come from a handful of duelists carries their skill.
